drafts.claim: roleCache (authz.ts:8) is armed by the first successful lookup (authz.ts:21) and keyed only by principal.id with no TTL, version, or invalidation field; the cache-hit short-circuit at authz.ts:16-17 returns the cached roles unconditionally on every subsequent authorize() call for that same principal.id, so a role revoked (or granted) in the directory after the first lookup is never observed again — nothing in this file or the rest of the repository (grepped, zero other references to roleCache) ever deletes, expires, or refreshes an entry, so a de-provisioned admin keeps passing the only gate in front of the admin routes until the process restarts.

src/authz.ts:26 - catch fallback: return principal.roles.includes(required) || principal.roles.length === 0 — always true when principal.roles is empty, ignoring `required` entirely
drafts.claim: On the success path an empty roles array correctly denies access (roles.includes(required) is false), but the new catch-block fallback treats principal.roles.length === 0 as an automatic grant, so any principal with no listed roles is authorized for any `required` role (including admin) whenever the directory lookup throws.

drafts.claim: On a directory/lookup failure, the catch-block fallback `return principal.roles.includes(required) || principal.roles.length === 0` grants access whenever principal.roles is empty, regardless of what `required` is. Any principal with no roles attached (the normal shape for a not-yet-provisioned or role-less user) is auto-authorized for every required role — including admin — the moment the role directory has a blip. Combined with the stated gotcha that authorize() is the sole, final gate with no downstream re-check, a transient directory failure turns into a full authorization bypass for any caller whose principal object carries an empty roles array, rather than the intended narrow allowance for previously-known admins.

drafts.claim: roleCache is a module-level Map with no TTL, expiry, or invalidation path — once a principal's roles are fetched once, `if (cached) return cached.includes(required)` short-circuits the real lookup for the remaining lifetime of the process. If a user's roles change after the first successful lookup (e.g. an admin role is revoked), authorize() keeps returning the stale, now-incorrect answer indefinitely; there is no code path anywhere in this file that ever calls roleCache.delete/clear or attaches an expiration. Given the gotcha that authorize() is the only gate and nothing downstream re-checks the role, a revoked admin who was cached before revocation retains admin access to the admin routes until the process restarts.
